messages:
nate (customer): Hi — my org's free credits dropped to -15 after a routine embedding call. Dashboard shows -15 free credits but the invoice is $0. I only made one request, didn't see any errors. Can someone explain how credits can go negative?

sara (support): Sorry about that, nate. Can you share your org id and a sample request/response (no secrets)? We'll open a ticket and look at consumption events.

nate (customer): Org: org_8Zk7f. Sample call (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-XXX" -d '{"model":"embed-v1","input":"hello"}'
```
Response headers included `x-free-credits-remaining: 5` at 2026-12-08T14:12:03Z then I made another call at 14:12:05 and afterwards dashboard showed -15. No retries from my side.

sara (support): Thanks — I've created ticket RB-3129 and escalated to billing. @liam can you check ledger/ingest for org_8Zk7f around 2026-12-08T14:12Z?

liam (billing): Looking now. Early note: I see two usage events ingested within ~1s for the same request-id: `req_01Gx2A`. One event has tokens=20, the other tokens=200. Both mapped to free-credit bucket. Suspect a replay/ingest duplication. Pulling raw ledger entries and message queue offsets.

nate (customer): I didn't retry. If it helps, client had a transient 502 right before second call but I didn't re-send. Could a replay from the gateway cause double-burn?

liam (billing): Possible. We're checking the ingestion dedupe window. If message bus redelivery happened and dedupe key (request-id) wasn't present or different, two events could apply.

devops-bot: Deployed log-collector job to pull raw events: offsets 4201-4224 from usage-ingest-prod for partition 3. Logs saved to /var/artifacts/RB-3129/ingest-trace.log

liam (billing): Pulled logs. I see two ingestion messages with identical body but different metadata.trace_id. Downstream dedupe relied on `request_id` header — one record had `request_id: req_01Gx2A` and the other had `request_id: null` due to a proxy strip. Both were accepted and applied to free pool.

sara (support): So that explains double application. What are remediation options?

liam (billing): We have two paths: 1) Manual ledger adjustment to restore 210 free credits (current negative -> 195 remaining), issue a corrective audit entry and update dashboards; 2) Replay a compensating event in the ingestion pipeline that will be ignored by downstream if dedupe fixed. Manual adjustment is faster. Need approval from finance for adjustments > $0 equivalent.

nate (customer): Manual fix is fine. How long to reflect on dashboard and does this affect invoices?

liam (billing): Dashboard will update within ~15 minutes after adjustment. No invoice impact — promo free credits are separate from billable invoiced usage; we'll add an audit note referencing RB-3129.

sara (support): Nate — we will schedule the manual credit reversal now and confirm when it's done. Can you confirm you want us to proceed? :thumbsup:

nate (customer): Please proceed. Thanks.

devops-bot: Action scheduled: billing.adjust_free_credits(org_8Zk7f, +210) at 2026-12-08T15:03:12Z. Job id: job_9c2f.

liam (billing): Adjustment applied. Audit id AUD-20261208-01 created. Dashboard shows free credit = 195 now. Please verify on your end, nate.

nate (customer): Verified — shows 195, thanks. Any plan to prevent this from happening again?

liam (billing): Short term: enable a stricter dedupe by inserting `request_id` enforcement at the ingestion proxy and add a 60s idempotency window. Long term: add an ingestion-level checksum + dedupe key that survives proxy header strips. Filed RB-3130 to track.

sara (support): Closing the support thread once documentation and RB-3130 are in progress. Nate, we'll follow up in 48h with postmortem summary.

nate (customer): Appreciate it.
